cast.name: Oak Grove Slim
cast.note: Hero. Cutout of the exact avatar file.

cast.name: Bill Tucker
cast.note: At Brittlebank Park, west side of town.

landmarks.desc: Built 1876, French Second Empire, red brick with a gold dome and clock tower. Previously listed on the National Register; not counted in the downtown district's 39 buildings.
landmarks.name: Posey County Courthouse
landmarks.source: NPS Form 10-900; position: OSM courthouse centroid

landmarks.desc: Arts and Crafts bandstand in Sherburne Park, on Water Street at the riverfront. Reddish-brown brick base with four corner piers, flared hipped roof of clay tile. The park was dedicated May 28, 1913, a memorial to Sherburne Cronbach (1886-1903).
landmarks.name: Sherburne Park Bandstand
landmarks.source: NPS Form 10-900; position: OSM Sherburne Park centroid

landmarks.desc: Concrete obelisk in Sherburne Park marking the high point of the 1937 flood waters. The Ohio River crested at 59.25 ft on the Mount Vernon gauge on February 2, 1937.
landmarks.name: 1937 Flood Monument

landmarks.desc: 126 E. Third Street. Neo-Classical, buff brick and Indiana limestone, four Roman Doric columns. Among the earliest WWI veterans monuments in Indiana; the auditorium seated 1,100, and the building sheltered 1937 flood refugees.
landmarks.name: Memorial Coliseum

landmarks.desc: 520 Main Street (now the City Hall Annex). Carnegie library, completed summer 1905, Neo-Classical with four Ionic columns. Andrew Carnegie donated $12,500 for the building and $1,400 for equipment.
landmarks.name: Alexandrian Public Library

landmarks.desc: 526 Main Street. Built 1893 for $7,295; Romanesque Revival with Queen Anne influences. One of the oldest city halls in continuous use in Indiana.
landmarks.name: City Hall, Police and Fire

landmarks.desc: 118 Main Street. Dedicated 1927 for Battery E, 139th Field Artillery, Indiana National Guard. The drill floor became a skating rink around 1970, later a teenage center.
landmarks.name: Armory

landmarks.desc: 131 W. Second Street. Built by the Masons in 1879; vaudeville, dances and boxing on the second floor. Mount Vernon High School played its first basketball game here.
landmarks.name: Opera House

landmarks.desc: 311 Main Street. Built 1893 by Henry Weiss of Evansville after a fire, Romanesque Revival, at a cost of $25,000. Declared one of the finest stores in the state at its grand opening in April 1894.
landmarks.name: Rosenbaum Brothers Store

landmarks.desc: 109 W. Water Street. Faces the Ohio River and Sherburne Park; the lodge was founded in December 1907 and the building contract was awarded in June 1917.
landmarks.name: Eagles Lodge #1717

landmarks.desc: West of Sherburne Park on the riverfront. Commemorates the pioneer McFadin families who settled McFadin's Bluff (William and Andrew McFadin, arrived 1805). Historical Society marker placed 1934.
landmarks.name: McFadin Cemetery Site

landmarks.desc: Mount Vernon High School Field, 700 Harriett Street — home field on the east side of town.
landmarks.name: Mount Vernon High School Field

landmarks.desc: An interpretive addition for the open world: stepped seating facing the Ohio at Water Street. Not a surveyed structure — placed for the game, labelled as such.
landmarks.name: Riverfront Amphitheater

landmarks.desc: Water tower on the north side of town.
landmarks.name: Water Tower (north)

landmarks.desc: Water tower across the river on the Kentucky side, south of the Ohio.
landmarks.name: Water Tower (south)

landmarks.desc: Water Street at the Ohio River. Normal pool here is about 342.5 ft NAVD88; the base flood elevation is 369.1 ft NAVD88. Use the flood slider to see what the water does at BFE.
landmarks.name: River Front and Water Street
landmarks.source: OSM tourist information; BFE per FEMA FIS 18129CV000A Table 9

note: Curated landmarks. Positions marked approx=true are placed from street addresses on the town street grid and cross-checked against OSM POIs; they are NOT surveyed. Descriptions are from NPS Form 10-900 (Mount Vernon Downtown Historic District, 2003) or OSM. Procedural models are interpretive, built from the written descriptions — no measured drawings were used.
